summary: Customer wants to replace or supplement manual HPLC sampling in dissolution testing with in-line fiber probes to follow dissolution of two active ingredients over time.

facts_stated.text: Customer is a quality control laboratory.
The test is on a tablet.
The tablet releases two active ingredients.
Today they draw samples from each vessel by hand at fixed times.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: Today we draw samples from each vessel by hand at fixed times

facts_stated.text: They analyse the samples by HPLC.
They want fiber probes in the vessels.
They want to follow how much of each ingredient has dissolved over time.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: follow how much of each ingredient has dissolved over time

facts_stated.text: They ask whether this is feasible.
They ask what should be checked first.

targets.purpose: identify and quantify both active ingredients

targets.enquiry_quote: how much of each ingredient has dissolved over time
dissolution tests on a tablet that releases two active ingredients

customer_premises.claim: Fiber probes in the vessels can follow how much of each active ingredient has dissolved over time.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: We would like fiber probes in the vessels to follow how much of each ingredient has dissolved over time.

customer_premises.claim: The proposed in-line fiber-probe measurement is feasible for their dissolution test.
Both active ingredients can be measured simultaneously in the dissolution medium.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: follow how much of each ingredient has dissolved over time

customer_premises.claim: In-line fiber probes can be installed in the dissolution vessels without disrupting the QC dissolution test.

unknowns: Identity and concentration range of the two active ingredients
Dissolution medium composition (buffer, pH, surfactants, etc.)
Excipients, undissolved particles, and potential interferences
Optical properties of the dissolution medium (clear, turbid, absorbing)
Vessel geometry, volume, path length, and probe installation point
Required accuracy, precision, detection limits, response time, and sampling frequency
Reference HPLC method details and validation status
Cleaning, fouling, and probe compatibility with the dissolution apparatus
Regulatory requirements for QC dissolution testing
Whether simultaneous quantification of both actives is required
